questions.question: Which of the following is a term used for species that are not natural residents of the local habitat, but are included in this system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Exotic.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Exotic Species **introduced to new environments often reset the ecological condition in that new habitat.
 
• It threatens the species that exist there.
 
• Hence they are often termed invasive species.
 
• These species compete with local native species for food and cause disease in them.
 
• Lakes and islands are vulnerable to extinction threats from introduced species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abiotic** are those components of the environment that are non-living and affects living organism and the functioning of the ecosystem.
 
• A **biome** is a distinct biogeographical unit consisting of a biological community that has formed in response to a shared regional climate. Biomes may span more than one continent.
 
• **Endemic** is a disease that is regularly found in a particular area or community and is difficult to get rid of. e.g. Chicken pox in UK

questions.question: If n is the energy level index for an atom, then for the M shell, n is equal to:
questions.solution:

__
 
• If n is the energy level index for an atom, then for the M shell, n is equal to 3.
 
• **Shell given = M, orbit number = 3.**
 
• The maximum number of electrons present in a shell is given by the formula **2n2.**
 
 
• Therefore, **2 × 32 = 18**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• The distribution of electrons into different orbits of an atom was suggested by Bohr and Bury. The orbits or shells are represented by the letters K, L, M, N,… or the numbers, n = 1, 2, 3, 4.
 
• The following rules are followed for writing the number of electrons in different energy levels or shells:
 
• The maximum number of electrons present in a shell is given by the formula 2n2, where ‘n’ is the orbit number or energy level index. 
 
• The general formula for filling electrons in the shell is 2(*n*2); where *n* is the number of the shell.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus transmitted primarily by Aedes mosquitoes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zika fever.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Zika fever is caused by a virus transmitted primarily by Aedes mosquitoes.

 
• Zika virus is primarily transmitted by the bite of an infected mosquito from the Aedes genus, mainly Aedes aegypti, in tropical and subtropical regions.
 
 
• Aedes mosquitoes usually bite during the day, peaking during early morning and late afternoon/evening.
 
• This is the same mosquito that transmits dengue, chikungunya and yellow fever.
 
 
 
• The incubation period (the time from exposure to symptoms) of Zika virus disease is estimated to be 3–14 days.
 
• The majority of people infected with Zika virus do not develop symptoms.
 
 
• Symptoms are generally mild including fever, rash, conjunctivitis, muscle and joint pain, malaise, and headache, and usually last for 2–7 days.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tularemia **is a bacterial disease in humans, wild, and domestic animals.
 
• **Malaria** is a parasitic disease spread by mosquitoes. Humans are infected with the parasite after being bitten by infected mosquitoes.
 
• **Minamata disease **is a disease of the central nervous system, a poisoning caused by long-term consumption, in large amounts, of fish and shellfish from Minamata Bay.
 
 
• The causative agent is** methylmercury.**

questions.question: What special name is given to the frictional force exerted by a fluid?

__
 
• Drag forces appear whenever there is motion in air or water or in any other fluid.
 
• The drag forces always act in the** opposite direction to fluid flow.**
 
• Example-Drag on a ship moving in the water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__​**

 
 

 
 
Drag

 
 
 
The frictional force exerted by fluids is also called drag

 
 
 

 
 
Buoyancy

 
 
 
An upward force exerted by any fluid to oppose the weight of an immersed object is called upthrust or buoyancy

 
 
 

 
 
Upthrust

 
 
 
An upward force exerted by any fluid to oppose the weight of an immersed object is called upthrust or buoyancy

 
 
 

 
 
Convection

 
 
 
Transfer of heat due to bulk movement of molecules in fluids such as liquid or gas is called convection.

questions.question: In which year was the Treaty of Bassein signed between Baji Rao II, the Maratha Peshwa of Poona in India, and the British?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1802__.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The treaty of** Bassein was signed on 31st December 1802.​ **
 
• ​It was signed between** East India Company and Baji Rao II.**
 
• ​Baji Rao II was the** Maratha Peshwa of Pune, and the treaty was signed after the battle of Poona.**
 
• ​This treaty led to the decisive victory of the British and it eventually led to the domination of the** East India Company and the dissolution of Maratha power.**
 
• ​Baji Rao accepted the subsidiary alliance imposed by Lord Wellesley.
 
• ​He lost his independence in return for the gaddi of Peshwa.
 
• ​An English force Arthur Wellesley entered Poona on **May 13, 1803, and Baji Rao was declared the Peshwa.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **​​​**This treaty was not acceptable to all Marathas chieftains and resulted in the Second Anglo-Maratha War.
